articles.title: Why Bridgewater's CIO Says AI's Human Extinction Risk Is Real
articles.summary: Greg Jensen was one of the earliest backers of both OpenAI and Anthropic, and at Bridgewater, where he is the managing chief investment officer, he leads the hedge fund's AI strategy. As an early adopter of the technology, he has a lot of thoughts on where things stand right now in terms of model capability and safety, as well as the broader economic impacts of AI. Just recently, he published an op-ed in the New York Times that proposed a “token tax,” to help mitigate the job losses that AI might cause. In today's conversation, Jensen tells us how Bridgewater is currently using AI, why there needs to be a stronger AI regulatory state, and why it feels like the AI discourse is starting to resemble the months before Covid-19 took over the world in 2020. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Reuters Institute Survey Shows ChatGPT Use Is Broad, but Daily Habits Remain Limited
articles.summary: ChatGPT is the most widely used generative AI tool in a six-country Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism survey, but the data also show a clear gap between trying the technology and making it part of a daily routine. Across Argentina, Denmark, France, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States, 22% of respondents reported using ChatGPT weekly on average. Daily use was substantially lower. That distinction matters for businesses assessing AI adoption. A large number of people may be familiar with ChatGPT, yet frequent use is not universal. The survey's central lesson is not simply that generative AI has reached a broad audience. It is that sustained, habitual use still depends on whether people can find useful, repeatable roles for it. The figures come from the Reuters Institute's analysis of public attitudes to generative AI in six countries.
